title: SE201 Lesson 2: Build the whole system, AI-native

scenes.text: Quick question to start. You're asking agents to build a whole app, not just one fix. What matters most? [pause] The smartest model? The longest prompt? Or a system the agents can read, check, and rebuild on their own? [pause] <emphasis>The system they can read.</emphasis> A smarter model still guesses when the project lives in someone's head. A long prompt is gone after one chat. What's written into the system is there for every run, and every agent.

data.question:
Agents are building a whole app.
What matters most?
data.why:
Written into
the system,
for every run.

scenes.text: In one oh one, the unit of work was one loop. Plan, build, verify. One fix. One feature. [pause] In two oh one, the unit of work is the system. Many parts. Many people. Years of history. And now, agents working in it right alongside the people.

data.caption: Many loops, many people, one system.

scenes.text: So what does A.I. native actually mean? Here's the definition this series uses. A system is A.I. native when agents and people can <emphasis>both</emphasis> read it, find their way around it, contribute to it, and rebuild it. [pause] Not only the person who wrote it. Not only whoever knows the history.

data.headline:
AI-native: agents and people
can both read it, navigate it,
contribute to it, and rebuild it.

scenes.text: That takes four things. One. Every page people read has a twin an agent can read: plain Markdown, an index of the whole system, and an agents file that says how to work there. Two. Specs and briefs are the source. Change the brief, and the build follows. Three. Tests and checks are the contract. An agent is done when the checks pass, not when it says it's done. And four. Every change goes to staging first, and a person approves it before it reaches production.

data.label: WHAT MAKES A SYSTEM AI-NATIVE
rows:
A twin agents can read: Markdown,
an index, an AGENTS.md
Specs and briefs are the source
Tests and checks are the contract

Staging, then a person approves
before production

scenes.text: And this isn't hypothetical. The site you're on right now is built exactly this way.

Every page has an index dot M D twin, and every folder has an agents dot M D file. There's an L L M S dot T X T that indexes the whole site, a machine-readable lesson catalog, and a read-only connector A.I. tools can plug into. [pause] The pages are generated from one content file, and the rebuild steps are written down, so an agent can regenerate every page.

data.label: CLARKHUANG.GITHUB.IO  ·  WHAT AN AGENT CAN READ
data.ask:
Read it, navigate it,
rebuild it.
data.punch: Plus a read-only connector AI tools can use.

scenes.text: And here's the part that matters most. Agents open pull requests into a staging branch. Staging is a full preview of the site, hidden from search. [pause] And only I merge into production.

data.headline: How a change ships here
items: An agent opens a pull request
It lands on staging, a full preview
Only the owner merges to production

scenes.text: Think of a kitchen with one great cook. The recipes are in their head. Only they know where everything is. And every plate waits on them.

left: Only they know where things are
right: The chef checks at the pass

scenes.text: Now picture a big restaurant kitchen. The recipes are written down. Every station is labeled. A cook on a brand new shift can work from the cards. [pause] And nothing leaves the pass until the head chef looks at it. That's what lets a kitchen grow past one great cook.

left: Only they know where things are
right: The chef checks at the pass

scenes.text: Now scale that up. An enterprise system isn't one repo. It's dozens of services, data that has to stay private, and people who need to know who changed what, and why. [pause] The same four things still hold. They just matter <emphasis>more</emphasis>. Without them, every agent starts from zero, and every person becomes the bottleneck.

data.label: THE SAME SYSTEM, BUILT TWO WAYS
data.reported:
Agents guess.
People become the bottleneck.
data.actually:
Agents read and check.
People decide.

scenes.text: That's the path for this series. Today: build the whole system, A.I. native. Then, decompose it into a graph. Run agents in parallel, and bring the work back together. Put people where the decisions matter. Measure quality, and watch it run. Turn repeated work into skills. Wire it into routines and pipelines. Then, agents that operate enterprise systems, with real permissions, and a full audit trail. [pause] And last, a capstone: one feature, built end to end.

data.label: SOFTWARE ENGINEERING 201  ·  FROM LOOP TO ENTERPRISE SYSTEMS
rows: Decompose the system into a graph

Capstone: one feature,
end to end

scenes.text: Which gives us rule two, for your agents. Before you build anything bigger than one fix, make it readable: a Markdown twin, an index, and an agents file. Keep the specs as the source, and the checks as the contract. And send every change through staging, for a person to approve before production.

scenes.text: Now, your turn. Pick a system you work on. If a brand new agent showed up tomorrow, what could it read? [pause] And what would it have to guess?
